sections.text: The Pure worship the true God; the Passionate, the powers of wealth and magic; the Ignorant, the spirits of the dead and of the lower orders of nature.
अशास्त्रविहितं घोरं तप्यन्ते ये तपो जनाः।
Those who practise austerities not commanded by scripture, who are slaves to hypocrisy and egotism, who are carried away by the fury of desire and passion,
They are ignorant. They torment the organs of the body; and they harass Me also, Who lives within. Know that they are devoted to evil.

So we had been discussing chapter 17, Sraddha Traya Vibhaga Yoga, three types of sraddha. The chapter opened with Arjunas question: if someone has not understood the Sastras, or even having understood, he sets aside the prescription in the Shastras, but has faith in what he thinks is right and is pursuing his faith -- does that faith be considered Sattvik, Rajasik, or Tamasic? Thats a simple question, simply because in the last chapter, the clear advice by Krishna is to follow the prescriptions of the Sastras in deciding what to do and what not to do. And as we have seen, Sastras literally means the collective wisdom of your culture, your society, your ancestors.
So unless I really rely on the wisdom of my ancestors, I will have no foundation to decide what is right and wrong. Any profession, any science -- you build on what has already been tried and true and proven in the labs or in workshops, and then say, now where do I go from here? So the clear prescription was not to ignore the wisdom of your ancestors, your civilization, your culture, and then decide what is right and wrong for you. Its not saying that you dont think yourself, but think based on the tried and true wisdom.
When we go to high school and learn chemistry and the teacher says H2O makes water, well, you have to have some faith in him. Unless you have faith, you will not learn, because you have faith in the teacher that you will accept that and then you will prove yourself going to the lab. So the prescription was follow the Sastras and decide what to do and not to do.
Arjunas question is, if someone completely sets aside the prescription in Sastras for lack of knowledge or lack of faith in the Sastras, but he has a faith in something he believes in, does that faith to be classified as Sattvik Rajasik or Tamasic? Because as we have seen, everything can be classified Sattvik, Rajasik, or Tamasic. Bhagavan said: Ill tell you, its not a one-label-fits-all type of answer. Your faith will be as you are.
My faith will be as per my experiences. Every time I walk into the airport, Im absolutely sure the plane will be on time -- if the last few times I went there the plane was on time, Ill say it will be on time. But if the last few times Id been going there it was always late, what will be my faith? Chances are my flight will be delayed.
So anytime Im going to India, what I do is I leave about six hours of gap between when I go from Richmond to New Jersey airport and New Jersey to Mumbai. We have no faith that the flight from Richmond to New Jersey will take me in time. They say, keep a two-hour gap.
No, no -- six hours gap. You dont want to miss an international flight. Thats my faith in our airline based on my experience.
And then the other people may have other things. So Bhagavan said that your faith is Sattva Anurupa. It in accordance with your own self, your own core of your being, core of your mind.
So my faith will be what my experiences are. Faith is something that comes intuitively to you, more like a tendency. Why do I like music? I dont know -- thats my tendency. But the more I follow my tendency, the more I will be following that path.
The more I have faith in the Gita, the more Gita I will read; the more I read the Gita, the more faith I have in it. So the two are wedded together. The more faith I have, the more I will pursue that path.
The more I pursue that path, the more my faith increases. So Bhagavan said, it is the individual who decides whether he will have faith which is Sattvik, Rajasic, or Tamasic, depending on the tendencies of his mind. Yajante Sattvika Devan -- so if the overall makeup of my mind is Sattvik, what will I do? Well, I will follow Sattvic beings.
I will strive to pursue or worship divine beings. My role models depend on my tendencies. If I am pursuing wealth, my role model is Bill Gates.
If I want to be a great leader, my role model will be Mahatma Gandhi. If I want to be spiritual, my role model will be a great sage or teacher. Depending on my faith, my role model would be different.
Thats as simple as that. So Bhagavan said: Sattvika Yajante Devan -- one whose makeup is Sattvik, predominantly Sattvik. These are not exclusive qualities of one person, one thing, or one being.
Everything is made up of some combination of Sattvik, Rajasik, and Tamasic. But if my mental makeup is predominantly Sattvik, I will be pursuing the Deva, the divine beings, Yaksa, Rakshansi, Rajasaha, those who are Rajasik will pursue or worship Yakshas and Rakshasas. From the Puranas we have the descriptions of Devas and Yakshas and Rakshasas, but its simply told here is Sattvik will follow the divine beings, Rajasik will follow the one which has wealth and power.
Yaksas are supposed to be wealthy beings. There is a story in Mahabharata 1 where Yudhishthir goes to this lake when he wants to drink water. That lake was controlled by a Yaksha.
Yaksha said, you cant drink water till you answer all my questions. If you answer all my questions, Ill let you take water. In other words, he was the controller of that lake.
He was wealthy enough to control his lake. These days people own islands because theyre wealthy. So the Yaksa that the wealthy beings, and here in Purana, I say theyre Kuberas brothers or cousins.
So theyre wealthy beings or Rakshasas immense power. There are stories in Puranas about Rakshasas immense power. In other words, even in society there will be people who are Sattvic and people who are wealthy and powerful.
So if my tendency is Rajasic, then I will be pursuing the wealthy and powerful. If my quality is Sattvik, Ill pursue the divine being. Preta Bhuta Ganas -- the others who have Tamasic qualities will pursue the Preta and Bhuta.
We obviously know from our vernacular languages that Preta and Bhuta are the dead spirits. Now in this society, if there are three people pursuing the same goal of making a million, the one with a Sattvik tendency will say: lets find some creative way which will help the society and at the same time create the wealth -- and thats how Ill make my million. The Rajasik will say: lets destroy my competition or take over someone else, and Ill get my million.
And the last one will say: lets pursue the lottery, buy the Mega Millions. All three have the same goal, but all three have a different avenue to reach there. Now all three are working hard to achieve the same goal -- making a million.
The Sattvic person is working very hard to achieve his goal creatively. The Rajasic is working just as hard but competitively. The Tamasic is also working hard but relying on chance.
Their means are different, depending on where their faith is. The one whos pursuing the lottery has complete faith that he cannot get a million in any other way -- this is the only way he can make a million. The one who wants to employ himself in a business has complete faith he can succeed that way.
And the Sattvic person has complete faith that if he creates something good for society, he will also benefit from it. Depending on your own experiences, your mental makeup is made. That mental makeup now defines where I have the faith in.
That faith will lead me into my actions. So Bhagavan said these faiths cannot be labeled simply because someone is not following Sastra. He may not know the Sastras but has Sattvic tendencies -- he will follow Sattva.
He may not know Sastras but has Rajasic tendencies -- he is following Rajasik. And he may not know Sastras because hes Tamasic -- hes following Tamas. So Preta and Bhuta are the dead spirits.
In other words, normal society will consider that to be a non-starter. Somebody says, well Rajan, why dont you buy a lottery? I never won anything in my life. Lets not waste my dollar.
At least I have a dollar. After that I wont have a dollar. But somebody has the faith and says, well, I have $10, Ill put nine of them in the lottery.
Im pretty much against the lottery, by the way, because were taxing the people who can afford the least in the society. They say lottery is good for education, it will reduce your taxes. No -- its a tax on the people who cannot afford that tax.
Most lottery tickets are bought by people who can least afford it. But they are following their faith. Asastra vihitam ghoram tapyante ye tapo janaha.
Now I have my faith that this is how I can pursue my goal. My faith is dependent on my experiences. So now Im pursuing my goal vigorously because Im as sincere as anybody else.
But Im pursuing it in a field which I think is the most conducive for me to achieve that -- not knowing what is right or wrong because I did not take time to find out. Im working very hard. As I said last time, I want to go to New Jersey, but Im driving as fast as I can on I-95 south just because I didnt take time to figure out whether New Jersey is north or south, without knowing what is right or wrong from the tried and true wisdom of my society.
If I had just taken the directions from AAA or a GPS, it would tell me New Jersey is to the north. But I didnt take it. I didnt want to take that time.
Theyre working very hard. They are pursuing these austerities vigorously. Dambha ahankara sanyuktaha -- because theyre filled with dambha, hypocrisy.
And ahankara, ego -- nobody knows better than I do. So who are they to tell me that New Jersey is to the north? I know its got to be this way. Ahankara sanyuktaha, Kama raga balanvitaha -- they are propelled to do this by what? Kama, desire, and raga, attachment.
Kama and raga are propelling my actions, and I think my happiness lies there. My goal is to achieve happiness, just as everybody elses is. But I think my happiness lies in these actions, where others are saying no -- thats where you have the danger that you probably will be unhappy.
We tell our kids: dont do that. But at that time the child does not think he is going to get hurt. But if he listens to you -- you as an elder person have learned from your own experience that jumping from that second floor is going to get you in trouble.
A young person, at the age of 8 or 9 or 10, thinks he can do anything he wants. Propelled by that desire and attachment, he wants to show off to his friend that he can jump from the second story. We have seen that in our childhood.
Hypocrisy and arrogance, the ego filled with that and propelled by attachment and desire. And they are putting vigorous actions in the fields which they consider appropriate for them. Karshayantaha Sarirastham bhutagramam a Chaitasaha.
This is a description of someone who has completely ignored the advice from the Sastras. We read the Bhagavad Gita every Sunday -- what do we do after that? The Bhagavad Gita says one thing, but thats not really what we follow. So now we fall into this category.
Knowing fully well, we set aside the prescription in the Shastra. We are propelled by our desire and our attachments, and also we are dambha ahankara sanyukta.

These verses present a sobering warning about misguided worship and extreme practices. Krishna describes those who, driven by hypocrisy (dambha), ego (ahankara), desire (kama), and attachment (raga), perform harsh austerities not prescribed by scriptures. Most striking is the statement that such people torment the organs of the body and harass Me also, Who lives within - revealing that when we abuse our body-mind complex through extreme or misguided practices, we are actually disrespecting the Divine that dwells within us. The sattvic worship Devas (divine beings representing light and wisdom), the rajasic pursue Yakshas and Rakshasas (representing wealth and power), while the tamasic follow spirits of the dead.
Examine your own spiritual practices and the role models you follow. Who are your Devas - the ideals and beings you worship through your attention and energy? If you seek wealth above all, your role model might be a billionaire; if wisdom, perhaps a sage; if power, perhaps a political figure. Today, notice when ego or the desire to show off enters your spiritual practice. Do you meditate to genuinely purify the mind, or partly to feel superior to others? Do you practice austerities that honor the body as a temple, or do you engage in extreme behaviors driven by pride or self-punishment? Ask yourself: Are my practices nourishing the Divine within, or harassing it?
